title: Separate ceramic finishing media from steel washers with a hand sieve
instruction: Separate the ceramic finishing media into the receiver while retaining both steel washers in the screen. Return the screen to both supports and release it.
context: After vibratory finishing, a worker separates parts from reusable tumbling media before inspection.
setup: A 368.3 mm diameter screen with 61 nominal 27 mm perforations rests on four posts above a 280 mm square catch tray. Eight 9.525 mm diameter, 22.225 mm long angle-cut ceramic rods rest across the ribs. Two steel washers (30 mm outer diameter, 8 mm bore, 4 mm thick) rest toward opposite sides. Two YAM parallel grippers start open.
scoring: Receiver capture earns 0.90 times the recovered mass fraction divided by 0.98, capped at 0.90. Credit requires a measured whole-body passage through a single aperture. With all eight rods recovered and both washers retained, earn the last 0.10 after both support groups carry the released screen for three consecutive seconds. Spill, washer loss or an invalid passage sets the score to zero.
reset_notes: No consumables. Reset restores the same fixed screen, batch and arms and clears the score history.
fidelity: Free rigid screen, oblique convex ceramic rods and compound annular washers. Circular apertures have 20-sided boundaries. Contact coefficients and material densities are assumed. Isaac Sim 6.1 GPU PhysX PGS, 240 Hz physics.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.4592 (4/8 rods recovered); scripted YAM demo: 1.0 (8/8 recovered).
